Nxeon VPS/game-server hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`), single Proxmox host, real production system — be careful, this touches live infrastructure and a real paying-adjacent customer.

## Background (already fully diagnosed, don't re-investigate this part)

A customer ("Animeboy Go2", user id `cmt9sllct000chlrxnkl727oo`) ordered a Terraria game server. It provisioned as Proxmox VM 109 (`terraria-i2ydef`, app `Server.id` = `cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx`), but got assigned IP `51.79.168.98` — which is the DEDICATED IP of a completely different, unrelated internal infrastructure VM (VMID 9010, the cold-email relay, hostname `coldemail-relay`). Root cause: `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s `syncDedicatedIpPool()` imported that IP into the customer-assignable pool as "FREE" without checking whether it already had an OVH Virtual MAC bound to it (it did — `02:00:00:93:2c:79`, already attached to VM 9010's `net0`). This has ALREADY been fixed in code (a `findVirtualMacForIp(address)` check was added before importing an IP as FREE — read the current `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` to see the fix in place) — your job is to deploy that fix and repair the one already-broken customer server, NOT to re-diagnose or re-fix the root cause.

Symptoms this caused on VM 109: `GAME_POWER` jobs failing with "no service unit found" (SSH landing on the relay VM instead), `GAME_UPDATE` failing with SSH connection timeouts, and "All configured authentication methods failed" — because two VMs are fighting over the same MAC/IP.

## What's already done for you

A new dedicated IP was ordered from OVH to replace the bad one: order id `22453814`, plan `ip-failover-arin`, $2.39 USD/month, placed via the cart-based OVH order API (`lib/ovh.ts`'s `ovh()`/`ovhApi` helpers — same pattern used for ordering IPs elsewhere in this codebase). As of the last check it had NOT yet appeared in `ovhApi.ips()`'s result — OVH IP delivery isn't always instant. The known baseline IPs on the account (do not treat any of these as the new one) are: `51.79.154.233`, `51.79.162.96`, `51.79.168.98`, `51.79.226.200`, `51.79.226.201`, `51.79.226.215` (plus 2 IPv6 entries). Poll `ovhApi.ips()` (reasonably spaced, e.g. every 1-2 minutes, not tight-looped) until a NEW address appears that isn't in that list.

## Your task, once the new IP appears

1. Run `syncDedicatedIpPool()` (from `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`) so the new IP gets imported into the `DedicatedIp` table as FREE (safe now with the fix in place — verify the fix code is actually present before relying on it).
2. Create a Virtual MAC for the new IP bound to VM 109 (`ovhApi.createVirtualMac(server, newIp, 'terraria-i2ydef')` — check `lib/ovh.ts` for the exact server name constant used elsewhere, likely `ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net`).
3. Update Proxmox VM 109's network config (`/etc/pve/qemu-server/109.conf`) — change `net0`'s MAC to the new virtual MAC and `ipconfig0`'s `ip=` to the new address (keep the same gateway, `gw=51.79.162.254`). **Do NOT touch VM 9010's config or anything about the cold-email relay — it must remain completely untouched throughout this task.** You can use `qm guest exec 9010 -- ...` style commands are for VM 9010 only if you ever need to double check its state for comparison — never write to it.
4. Reboot VM 109 (`qm reboot 109` or equivalent) so the new network config takes effect, then verify: SSH reachability to the new IP, and that Terraria's game service is actually running there (check what systemd unit name the game-control worker expects — look at `worker/game-control.ts` / `lib/game-config.ts` for how Terraria's service unit is named/managed, and confirm it's actually present and healthy on VM 109 now that networking is fixed — the "no service unit found" errors might resolve entirely once traffic reliably reaches the right box, but verify, don't assume).
5. Update the app's `Server` row (`cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx`) — set `ipAddress` to the new address (and any related fields like `vmid`/`nodeId` if you find they're also stale/wrong — investigate the current row's `nodeId` being blank too, and fix if it's part of the same underlying issue; check how properly-provisioned servers set `nodeId` for comparison, e.g. look at another working `Server` row).
6. Clean up the bad `DedicatedIp` row for `51.79.168.98` (currently `serverId` = Animeboy's server, `virtualMac` = the relay's MAC) — it should never have existed in the customer pool at all. Either delete it or clear `serverId`/mark it in a way that makes clear it's reserved for internal infra and permanently excluded from customer allocation (your judgment on the cleanest fix given the schema — `DedicatedIpStatus` enum, check its values).
7. Verify the fix end-to-end: retrigger a `GAME_POWER` (start/restart) job for this server through whatever the normal app path is (check `lib/actions-*.ts` for the game power-action server action, or the `Job` table/worker sweep that processes `GAME_POWER` jobs) and confirm it now succeeds.
8. Reply to the customer's support ticket. It's a live-chat conversation (`ChatConversation.id` = `cmt9tp22i002dhlrxk9gfawax`, `ChatMessage` model, `sender: "agent"` for a human/staff reply — see `lib/actions-chat.ts`'s `replyToConversation()` for the exact transaction shape: creates a ChatMessage + updates ChatConversation status/unread flags + a Notification if the visitor has a userId). That function requires an authenticated staff session (`requireArea("support")`), which you won't have as a script — replicate its exact DB transaction directly instead. He originally asked "Can I get a refund?" and "I can't connect to the server" and got two AI-degraded-mode failure messages. **The owner explicitly said: no refund, just fix the server** — so don't offer or process any refund. Write a warm, honest, human-toned reply: acknowledge the connection issue was real and on Nxeon's end (an IP conflict, not anything he did), and that it's fixed now — his server should be reachable. Keep it natural, not corporate-templated.

## Deploy the code fix

The `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` fix is currently sitting as an uncommitted change directly in `/opt/nxeon`'s working tree (not yet committed). Follow the established deploy pattern used throughout this session:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git diff lib/dedicated-ip.ts > /tmp/dedicated-ip-fix.diff
git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-dipfix -b hotfix/dedicated-ip-pool-mac-check
cd /opt/nxeon-wt-dipfix && git apply /tmp/dedicated-ip-fix.diff
ln -sfn /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules && ln -sf /opt/nxeon/.env .env
npm run build   # must pass
```
Commit with a clear message, then back in `/opt/nxeon`: confirm `git diff lib/dedicated-ip.ts` is byte-identical to the worktree's committed diff, `git checkout -- lib/dedicated-ip.ts` to discard the now-redundant uncommitted copy, `git merge --ff-only <the hotfix branch>`, clean up the worktree/branch. Then sync `/opt/nxeon-staging` (`git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/main`, `npm run build`, restart `nxeon-staging-web.service`, curl-verify HTTP 200), then run `bash scripts/promote-production.sh` to ship it live (both web and worker restart — the worker is what actually runs `syncDedicatedIpPool`, so it needs the new code to avoid ever reimporting a bad IP again). This is a safety-only fix (prevents a future collision), low risk, fine to promote straight through without asking — the DB/VM-level repair work in steps 1-8 above is the sensitive part, be careful there.

## Ground rules

- Never touch VM 9010 (the cold-email relay) in any way.
- This is a real customer server — verify each step actually worked before moving to the next, don't assume.
- If you get stuck or something looks ambiguous/risky (e.g. the game service genuinely isn't installed on VM 109 and needs real re-provisioning, not just a network fix), stop and report clearly rather than guessing further.
- Report back: what you found, what you fixed, the verification evidence for each step, the exact reply you sent to the customer, and the deploy commit hash.
